about.body.explanation: About paragraph: the product is built by Task Runner Technology LTD, a British company; belief that every shop anywhere deserves a good point of sale. Company identity statement, keep the legal name and country.

android.cta.explanation: Primary button on the Android page: download the Android app.

android.cta2.explanation: Secondary link on the Android page: jump to the set-up steps.

android.faq.a1.explanation: Android FAQ answer 1: not to sell; a sale completes with no connection; Wi-Fi is needed to work with other tills on the shop's network.

android.faq.a2.explanation: Android FAQ answer 2: yes, every version runs the same till; the tablet can be the main till or join a main till on another platform.

android.faq.a3.explanation: Android FAQ answer 3: not yet; download from our site; Android warns the first time because the app is from outside Google Play, which is expected.

android.faq.a4.explanation: Android FAQ answer 4: Android 7.0 or newer; a 64-bit version for most tablets, one for older 32-bit tablets, a universal one when unsure.

android.faq.q1.explanation: Android FAQ question 1: does the tablet need Wi-Fi or mobile data.

android.faq.q2.explanation: Android FAQ question 2: can an Android tablet work alongside a Windows or Raspberry Pi till.

android.faq.q3.explanation: Android FAQ question 3: is it on Google Play.

android.faq.q4.explanation: Android FAQ question 4: which tablets does it run on.

android.faq.title.explanation: Heading of the FAQ on the Android page.

android.lede.explanation: Intro paragraph of the Android page: the whole till runs on the tablet so a sale completes offline; free.

android.limits.i1.explanation: Limitation: the app is not on Google Play yet, it is downloaded from this website.

android.limits.i2.explanation: Limitation: Android does not let an app replace itself silently, so every update needs one tap in Android's installer.

android.limits.i3.explanation: Limitation: an Android till joined to a main till does not update itself to match; install the new version by hand.

android.limits.i4.explanation: Limitation: card payments go through the shop's own card machine and provider, which may need its own connection.

android.limits.i5.explanation: Limitation: screen pinning is Android's standard pin; it starts only after the user accepts Android's prompt, and someone who knows Android's unpin gesture can leave it. Security-relevant, keep accurate.

android.limits.t.explanation: Heading of the limitations list on the Android page.

android.note.explanation: Small note under the Android buttons: Android 7.0 or newer, installed from our website, not yet from Google Play.

android.setup.s1.explanation: Android step 1: open the download page on the tablet and tap the Android app; most tablets need the 64-bit version which the page picks automatically.

android.setup.s2.explanation: Android step 2: allow installing from unknown sources when Android asks; Play Protect may say it has not seen the app before, tap Scan app, then continue. Button names must match Android's wording in the target language.

android.setup.s3.explanation: Android step 3: open Universal Till and follow the setup (language, country, shop name), then add products.

android.setup.steps.t.explanation: Sub-heading above the numbered Android set-up steps.

android.setup.title.explanation: Heading of the Android set-up section.

android.shot.explanation: Caption and image alt text of the Android sale-screen screenshot: the sale screen is the same on a tablet as on every other till.

android.title.explanation: Main heading of the Android till page.

android.what.bt.d.explanation: Feature text: pair a Bluetooth barcode scanner or scale from inside the till; Android asks once to allow Bluetooth.

android.what.bt.t.explanation: Feature title: Bluetooth scanners and scales.

android.what.kiosk.d.explanation: Feature text: set a tablet to self-order so customers order themselves; the till asks Android to pin the screen, which blocks the Home and Back buttons.

android.what.multi.d.explanation: Feature text: an Android tablet can be the main till or join another till on the shop's network; sales sync between them.

android.what.multi.t.explanation: Feature title: one till or several.

android.what.offline.d.explanation: Feature text: everything is stored on the tablet; if Wi-Fi drops the status bar says so and sales continue.

android.what.same.d.explanation: Feature text: the Android app runs the very same till as Windows, Mac and Raspberry Pi: sale screen, catalogue, stock, receipts and so on.

android.what.same.t.explanation: Feature title: the same till, not a cut-down app.

android.what.title.explanation: Heading of the section listing what an Android tablet till offers.

android.what.update.d.explanation: Feature text: when a new version is out tap the update chip and confirm in Android's own installer; the first time Android also asks for permission. 'Update chip' must match the till's status-bar label.

android.what.update.t.explanation: Feature title: updates from inside the till.

close.cta.explanation: Button of the closing block: start free (links to the Find your setup wizard).

close.talk.explanation: Lead-in text before a contact link/email address: 'Or talk to a person:'. Ends with a colon; the address follows.

close.title.explanation: Heading of the closing call-to-action block on the home page.

consent.accept.explanation: Consent banner button: accept analytics cookies. Must be as visually and verbally equal to Reject as the original.

consent.label.explanation: Accessible name (aria-label, read by screen readers only) of the cookie consent banner. One word.

consent.privacy.explanation: Link in the consent banner to the privacy policy.

consent.reject.explanation: Consent banner button: reject analytics cookies. Must be as easy and clear as Accept.

consent.text.explanation: Cookie consent banner text: we would like to use Google Analytics cookies to see how visitors use the site; nothing is set unless the visitor accepts. Consent wording, keep the 'nothing is set unless you accept' promise exact. 'Google Analytics' is a brand name.

cta.btn.explanation: Button label of the final call-to-action band: get started. Currently not referenced by any page (kept because it is in every locale dictionary).

cta.lede.explanation: Text of the final call-to-action band: free forever for a single till; download today. Pricing claim, keep exact.

cta.title.explanation: Heading of the final call-to-action band.

dl.android.armv7.explanation: Download link label: Android app for older 32-bit devices.

dl.android.d.explanation: Download card text: Android 7.0 or newer; installed from the website, not Google Play.

dl.android.note.explanation: Note under the Android download: Android warns about 'unknown sources' the first time, which is expected for an app from outside Google Play and not a sign of danger. dl.android.universal.explanation: Download link label: the larger universal Android app for people unsure which to pick.

dl.note.windows.explanation: Note for the detected-Windows download: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, guided installer.

dl.os.android.explanation: Operating system name in the platform selector. 'Android' is a brand name.

dl.os.pi.explanation: Platform selector label for Raspberry Pi and other ARM64 boards.

dl.os.windows.explanation: Operating system name in the platform selector. 'Windows' is a brand name.

dl.others.explanation: Small sub-heading above the list of all downloads on every platform.

dl.pi.d.explanation: Download card text: Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 running 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS.

dl.pi.deb.explanation: Download link label: Raspberry Pi package. '.deb' extension, keep it.

dl.pilotlink.explanation: Link on the download page offering assisted setup via the free pilot instead. Arrow is a visual cue.

dl.primary.explanation: Label on the main (detected-platform) download button. One word.

dl.steps.explanation: Link to the three-steps getting started guide.

dl.sub.explanation: Sub-heading of the download page: free and offline-first; a best-guess device is preselected.

dl.title.explanation: Main heading of the download page.

dl.version.prefix.explanation: Text before the latest version number on the download page, for example 'Latest version: 1.2.3'. Ends with a colon and a space; the page appends the number.

dl.win.d.explanation: Download card text: supported Windows versions (10 or 11, 64-bit).

dl.win.exe.explanation: Download link label: Windows installer. '.exe' is a file extension, keep it.

faq.a1.explanation: FAQ answer 1: yes; EPOS, POS, till system and cash register all mean the same selling software.

faq.a2.explanation: FAQ answer 2: the till is free forever on own hardware, open source under the MIT licence, no monthly fee for the core; paid plans only cover cloud and services. Pricing and licence claims, keep exact.

faq.a3.explanation: FAQ answer 3: yes, a full sale completes offline; syncing is a bonus; card payments may need a connection depending on the provider.

faq.a4.explanation: FAQ answer 4: Raspberry Pi, old PC or laptop, mini-PC, touch terminal; downloads for Windows, macOS, Linux, Raspberry Pi and Android. Also states the iPhone and iPad apps are in internal testing (not on the App Store) and that a DIY till costs from about 70 pounds. Availability and price claims, keep exact.

faq.a5.explanation: FAQ answer 5: yes, any card machine and processor; we are never in the money flow, no fee creep, no frozen payouts. Pricing claim.

faq.a6.explanation: FAQ answer 6: export from the current system and import; Loyverse, Square, SumUp and Shopify exports are recognised automatically.

faq.q1.explanation: FAQ question 1 (also used in structured data for search engines): whether Universal Till is an EPOS system.

faq.q2.explanation: FAQ question 2: is it really free.

faq.q3.explanation: FAQ question 3: does it work without internet.

faq.q4.explanation: FAQ question 4: what hardware is needed.

faq.q5.explanation: FAQ question 5: can the shop take card payments.

faq.q6.explanation: FAQ question 6: can the shop move over from its current till.

faq.sub.explanation: Sub-heading of the FAQ: explains the words EPOS, POS, till system and cash register as search terms and names the two topics, what it is and what it costs.

faq.title.explanation: Heading of the home page FAQ section.

foot.privacy.explanation: Footer link to the privacy policy page.

foot.terms.explanation: Footer link to the terms of use page.

free.body.explanation: Paragraph listing what is included free (tables, kitchen screens, self-order kiosk, stock, staff and shifts, promotions, vouchers, reports, an AI assistant that uses the shop's own AI provider key). Pricing claim, keep the list exact.

free.cta.explanation: Link in the free section to the plan finder (Find your setup). Arrow is a visual cue.

free.pay.explanation: Sentence under the free list: anything running in the shop is free; the shop only pays for our cloud and our people. Pricing claim.

free.title.explanation: Heading of the 'free' section on the home page: a promise that free really is free.

hero.cta1.explanation: Primary hero button: start free (links to the Find your setup wizard, which leads to the download).

hero.cta2.explanation: Secondary hero button: opens the source code repository on GitHub.

hero.lede.explanation: Hero paragraph on the home page: never stops selling, runs on hardware the shop already owns, costs nothing to start, no minimum term on monthly billing except Germany's managed TSE line (the exception stays in the same sentence). Pricing claims, keep exact.

hero.note.explanation: Small note under the hero buttons, three facts separated by middle dots: MIT licensed, one small binary, works today. 'MIT' is a licence name, keep it.

meta.android-till.title.explanation: Browser-tab title and search headline of the Android till page. Keep 'Universal Till' and the product name Android.

sol.hospitality.d.explanation: Card text for hospitality: held orders, split payments, fast repeat items, kitchen workflow through plugins.

sol.market.d.explanation: Card text for market stalls: runs on a cheap phone-sized budget, needs no signal, easy to pack up and move.

start.cta.explanation: Button on the Getting started page: go to the download page.

start.dev.pc.d.explanation: Device card text: any 64-bit Windows or Linux machine works; gives an old computer a second life.

start.lx.3.explanation: Linux step 3: the browser opens the setup screen.

start.mac.3.explanation: macOS step 3: the browser opens the setup screen.

start.mac.t.explanation: macOS install block title, with an emoji icon. Keep the emoji and 'macOS'.

start.pi.t.explanation: Raspberry Pi / Debian install block title, with an emoji icon.

start.s1.d.explanation: Step 1 text: Universal Till is one small app that runs on hardware the shop already owns.

start.s1.t.explanation: Step 1 heading, with its number: choose a device. Keep the number and the middle dot.

start.s2.d.explanation: Step 2 text: download the version for the device from the download page then follow the steps for the system; every install opens the setup screen.

start.s2.t.explanation: Step 2 heading, with its number: install the app.

start.s3.d.explanation: Step 3 text: the first start opens a short wizard.

start.s3.t.explanation: Step 3 heading, with its number: follow the setup wizard.

start.s4.d.explanation: Step 4 text: add a few products and ring up the first sale.

start.s4.t.explanation: Step 4 heading, with its number: start selling.

start.sell.add.d.explanation: Card text: add items by hand or import a CSV; Loyverse and Square exports are recognised automatically.

start.sell.grow.d.explanation: Card text: scan a QR code to add a second till; tills sync over the shop's own network, free of charge.

start.sell.plug.d.explanation: Card text: open the plugin store for payments, loyalty, themes and more; verified, one-click install.

start.sell.ring.d.explanation: Card text: scan a barcode or tap a product tile, take cash or card, print or skip the receipt.

start.sell.ring.t.explanation: Card title: ring up a sale.

start.title.explanation: Main heading of the Getting started page.

start.w1.t.explanation: Setup wizard item title: your language.

start.w2.t.explanation: Setup wizard item title: your country.

start.w3.d.explanation: Setup wizard item text: name the shop and choose an admin PIN, then it is ready.

start.w3.t.explanation: Setup wizard item title: shop name and PIN.

start.win.1.explanation: Windows step 1: download the installer; '.exe' is a file extension, keep it.

start.win.2.explanation: Windows step 2: double-click and follow the wizard; it adds Start-menu and desktop shortcuts.

start.win.3.explanation: Windows step 3: open the app from the shortcut; the browser shows the setup screen.

start.win.t.explanation: Windows install block title, with an emoji icon. Keep the emoji.

switch.body.explanation: Paragraph: import products from Loyverse, Square, SumUp, Shopify or a spreadsheet; a preview is shown before anything is saved. Competitor names are brand names.

switch.pro.explanation: Sentence: on the Pro plan we do the move for the shop.

switch.side.explanation: Sentence: run Universal Till next to the old till until the shop is sure.

switch.title.explanation: Heading of the 'switch' section: moving from another till takes an afternoon.

tour.catalog.explanation: Screenshot caption title: the whole catalogue.

tour.catalog.d.explanation: Screenshot caption text: barcodes, variants, photos, tax and price.

tour.inventory.explanation: Screenshot caption title: stock you can trust.

tour.inventory.d.explanation: Screenshot caption text: receive, adjust, low-stock alerts, returns.

tour.lang.explanation: Screenshot caption title: speaks your language.

tour.lang.d.explanation: Screenshot caption text: lists some supported languages and notes right-to-left support. The language list is a statement of fact about the product; keep it consistent with what ships.

tour.plugins.explanation: Screenshot caption title: a signed plugin store.

tour.plugins.d.explanation: Screenshot caption text: payments, loyalty, themes; verified, one-click.

tour.sale.explanation: Screenshot caption title: the fast touch sale screen.

tour.sub.explanation: Sub-heading of the tour: real screens from a running till, not mock-ups.

tour.title.explanation: Heading of the screenshots tour section.

why.exit.d.explanation: Benefit text: no minimum term on monthly billing, cancel any month, take all data away free of charge; the one exception is Germany's managed TSE line, which has a minimum in months per activated main till (merchant terms clause 6; the number comes from the price file). Contract/pricing claim, keep exact.

why.exit.t.explanation: Benefit title: the plan itself never ties the shop in; the body (why.exit.d) names Germany's managed TSE line as the one exception.

why.hardware.d.explanation: Benefit text: old PC, laptop, Raspberry Pi, Android tablet or phone; unlimited tills, never charged per till.

why.hardware.t.explanation: Benefit title: use hardware you already have. Short sentence.

why.offline.d.explanation: Benefit text: a full sale works with no internet; tills catch up with each other when they reconnect.

why.payments.d.explanation: Benefit text: SumUp, Stripe or any standalone card machine; we never take a cut of the shop's takings. Pricing claim, keep exact.

why.payments.t.explanation: Benefit title: keep your own card provider.

why.title.explanation: Heading of the 'Why shops switch' section on the home page.

wiz.back.explanation: Wizard button: go to the previous question. Short, one word if possible.

wiz.cta.cloud.explanation: Result button: create a cloud account or sign in. Fits on one line in a button.

wiz.cta.download.explanation: Primary result button: download the free local app.

wiz.cta.talk.explanation: Result button: opens an email draft to us with the visitor's answers (mailto link).

wiz.edit.explanation: Button on the result screen: return to the questions to change answers.

wiz.finish.explanation: Wizard button on the last question: calculate and show the recommended setup (plan, hardware, plugins).

wiz.gap.cardother.explanation: Honesty note: we only have plugins for SumUp and Stripe; asks which provider the visitor uses.

wiz.gap.fiscalother.explanation: Honesty note for countries outside the supported fiscal rules: we do not support the visitor's country's fiscal rules yet and they must check their own legal requirements. Legal-sensitive.

wiz.gap.online.explanation: Honesty note: online ordering and web-shop sync are coming but not available, no date can be given; invites the visitor to tell us what they need.

wiz.gap.team.explanation: Honesty note: accountant access and phone support are not available yet; fixed staff roles are free on every plan, only custom roles are on the Pro plan.

wiz.gap.tr.explanation: Honesty note for Turkey: Turkish fiscal certification is unfinished, so we cannot promise legal Turkish receipts today. Legal-sensitive, must not be weakened.

wiz.hw.devices.explanation: Link text in the hardware block, to the Getting started page, which lists device options.

wiz.hw.have.explanation: Hardware advice when the visitor owns a device: any PC, laptop, Raspberry Pi, Android tablet or touch terminal works.

wiz.hw.need.explanation: Hardware advice when the visitor owns no device: our hardware shop is not open yet; a complete do-it-yourself till costs from about 70 pounds. Contains a price claim; keep the amount and currency exactly (use the local convention for the symbol position).

wiz.lede.explanation: Intro paragraph under the wizard heading. Sets the expectation that it is a short questionnaire (about a minute) leading to a plan, hardware and plugin recommendation. Friendly, 'we' voice.

wiz.n.cafe.explanation: Note for cafes: works offline so a Wi-Fi drop never stops a sale.

wiz.n.cardnone.explanation: Note for shops without card payments: start with cash, add SumUp or Stripe later from the plugin marketplace.

wiz.n.deowndevice.explanation: Note for Germany: the visitor may stay on the Local or Local Plus plan using their own approved fiscal device. Legal-sensitive.

wiz.n.detsemin.explanation:
Note for Germany: law requires a TSE (certified fiscal security device) for every business whatever till is used; Local and Local Plus users bring their own, from Shop a managed one is {tse} per month excluding VAT per main till; that managed line has a minimum term of {months} months for each activated main till and the plan itself has none (merchant terms clause 6); the free app is therefore not zero cost in Germany. {tse} is a formatted amount and {months} a whole number, both supplied by the page. Legal and pricing sensitive.

Placeholders:
- 1: {tse} — a ready formatted monthly price for the managed fiscal device, supplied by the page
- 2: {months} — the whole number of months of the minimum term, supplied by the page from the price file

wiz.n.restaurant.explanation: Note for restaurants and bars: table plan, kitchen screen and self-order are included free.

wiz.n.retail.explanation: Note for shops: barcodes, variants and stock tracking free; catalogue import from CSV or Excel.

wiz.n.salon.explanation: Note for barbers and salons: staff accounts and shifts free; booking platform sync (such as Booksy) not available yet.

wiz.n.stall.explanation: Note for market stalls: runs on an Android tablet or phone, keeps selling without signal.

wiz.n.ukfiscal.explanation: Note for the UK: there is no fiscal-device requirement. Legal statement about UK law; keep exact.

wiz.short.free.d.explanation: One-line caption under the 'download the free app' shortcut. Claims: runs on the shop's own computer, works offline, no monthly fee.

wiz.short.title.explanation: Heading of the shortcut box above the wizard for visitors who already know what they want.

wiz.skiphint.explanation: Small hint under a question: answering is optional, the visitor may leave it blank and continue.

wiz.step.explanation:
Progress text above each wizard question, for example 'Step 2 of 6'.

Placeholders:
- 1: {n} — the number of the current step, a whole number starting at 1
- 2: {total} — the total number of questions, a whole number

wiz.talk.intro.explanation: First line of the pre-filled email body, followed by the visitor's answers. Plain text.

wiz.talk.note.explanation: Note next to the 'Talk to us' button: it opens the visitor's own email app with answers filled in and nothing is sent unless they send it. Privacy-relevant, keep factually exact.

wiz.talk.plan.explanation: Label in the pre-filled email for the suggested plan, followed by the plan name. Plain text.

wiz.talk.subject.explanation: Subject line of the pre-filled email created by the 'Talk to us' button. Plain text, no markup.

wiz.title.explanation: Main heading (h1) of the Find your setup wizard page. A plain, inviting question-style promise.
